note: Partial Spearman computed via rank-based formula r_xy.z = (r_xy - r_xz*r_yz)/sqrt((1-r_xz^2)(1-r_yz^2)); p-value from t-test with df=n-3.

seiz_vs_auc_given_isi.interpretation: Seizure count vs AUC controlling for ISI. If p > 0.05, seizure count has no independent effect beyond ISI.

isi_vs_auc_given_seiz.interpretation: ISI vs AUC controlling for seizure count. If p < 0.05, ISI has independent predictive value beyond seizure count.

conclusion: Seizure count (marginal rho=-0.587, p=0.0026) and ISI (marginal rho=0.719, p=0.0001) are strongly co-correlated with each other (rho=-0.651, p=0.0006). After controlling for ISI, seizure count is no longer independently significant (partial rho=-0.224, p=0.3034). ISI remains independently predictive after controlling for seizure count (partial rho=0.548, p=0.0067). This suggests ISI is the more fundamental predictor; seizure count's apparent effect is largely mediated through ISI.
